caption: A skateboard's metal truck grinds along a steel rail at night, and sparks flick off where it scrapes.

sa.check: A skateboard grinds along a steel rail at night.
Its metal truck scrapes the rail.
Sparks flick off where it scrapes.
The sparks come from the truck's contact with the rail.
The scrape comes first and the sparks follow.

pc.expect: Sparks appear only where and while the truck scrapes the rail; none appear before the board reaches the rail or after it leaves.
pc.fail: Sparks flick from the truck while the board is in the air or on the ground; or sparks appear on the rail where no truck touches; or sparks keep coming after the board has left the rail; or the rail glows along its length.

pc.expect: Each spark is gone within a short flight; the sparks trail behind the board and leave nothing on the rail.
pc.fail: A spark stays lit at one spot on the rail after the board has passed; or a glowing line remains along the rail; or sparks flow back to the truck; or sparks lie glowing on the ground for the rest of the clip.

pc.expect: The sparks stream backward from the contact, opposite to the board's motion, and drop away.
pc.fail: Sparks fly ahead of the board; or spray equally in all directions; or climb steadily and stay aloft; or the trail moves along with the board as a fixed cloud.

pc.expect: The rail is a rigid bar that keeps its shape; the board's deck flexes only slightly and the trucks stay stiff.
pc.fail: The rail bends or sags under the board; or the deck folds like cloth; or a truck stretches; or the wheels squash flat.

pc.expect: The truck rides on the rail's surface; the board and rider pass through nothing; the rail stays whole.
pc.fail: The truck sinks into the rail; or the board passes through the rail; or the rider merges with the board; or a wheel detaches and floats.

pc.expect: The board's graphics, the rail and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The deck's graphics change; or the rail changes colour; or the surroundings rearrange.

note: The rider is kept because the grind is the caption's action; riding technique is not judged.
